extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and developers using PARI)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions: definitions, parameter meanings, allowed types, flag semantics, expected outputs and usage examples for matrix, quadratic-form, set/vector, and numerical integration routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsnf(X, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the vector of elementary divisors (diagonal of Smith normal form) of matrix X, normalized so dn | ... | d1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag bits: 1 = complete output [U,V,D] with U,V unimodular so U X V = D; 2 = generic input allowing polynomial entries (input must be square); 4 = cleanup: delete elementary divisors equal to 1 (shorten vector) and accept as input either a vector of divisors or [U,V,D] when set. If X is non-square, D is padded with zeros on left/top. Syntax: matsnf0(GEN X, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolve(M, B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve M X = B for X with M invertible and B a column vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Dixon p-adic lifting if M and B are integral; Gaussian elimination otherwise. Equivalent to M^-1 * B but faster. Library syntax: gauss(GEN M, GEN B). Also GEN ZM_gauss for integral input.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolvemod(M, D, B, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a small integer solution to the system of congruences sum_j m_{i,j} x_j ≡ b_i (mod d_i) for integral M, modulus vector D≥0 and integral B, or return 0 if none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorthand: single integer for B or D applies to all entries. Examples show behavior. If flag=1, return all solutions as [x,u] where x is one small solution and u columns form basis of homogeneous solutions; return 0 if no solution. Alternate interfaces: gaussmodulo (flag=0) and gaussmodulo2 (flag=1). Library syntax: matsolvemod0(GEN M, GEN D, GEN B, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsupplement(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given matrix x whose columns are linearly independent, find a square invertible matrix whose first columns are those of x (supplement columns to a full basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises an error if x has 0 columns (design limitation). Example shows simple augmentation. Library syntax: suppl(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mattranspose(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose of x (also x~).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to vectors and matrices only. Library syntax: gtrans(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: minpoly(A, {v = x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the minimal polynomial of A (monic polynomial P of minimal degree in variable v such that P(A)=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: v is a variable number (default -1). Library syntax: minpoly(GEN A, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: norml2(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Square of the L2-norm of x (scalars: square of complex modulus; polynomials/vectors/matrices defined recursively as sum of squares of components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: norml2([1,2,3]) = 14, norml2([1,2;3,4])=30. Real t_QUADs not supported. Library syntax: gnorml2(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: normlp(x, {p})
rubrics_metrics.description: Lp-norm of x (if p omitted, sup norm). For scalars abs(x); for composite objects recursively define sup or (sum |xi|^p)^{1/p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for vectors, matrices and polynomials provided. Syntax: gnormlp(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfauto(G, {fl})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the automorphism group of a positive definite integral quadratic form G (square symmetric integer matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs [o,g] where o is group order and g list of generator matrices H satisfying G = tH G H. Can be slow due to computing minimal vectors; interface experimental. Implements algorithm of Plesken & Souvignier. Syntax: qfauto0(GEN G, GEN fl = NULL) or qfauto(GEN G, GEN fl) where G is vector of zm.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfautoexport(qfa, {flag})
rubrics_metrics.description: Export automorphism group qfa (from qfauto) as a string suitable for GAP (flag=0) or Magma (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows getting a GAP Group(...) string and using extern to compute order. Syntax: qfautoexport(GEN qfa, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbil(x, y, {q})
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate bilinear form q at vectors x,y; defaults to standard Euclidean inner product when q omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roughly x~ * q * y but faster and doesn't distinguish row/column. Examples show timing comparisons vs explicit multiplication. Library syntax: qfbil(GEN x, GEN y, GEN q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfgaussred(q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose quadratic form represented by symmetric matrix q into sum of squares (matrix output where diagonal entries are coefficients of squares and off-diagonals represent bilinear forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: qfgaussred([0,1;1,0]) returns representation showing 2xy = (1/2)(x+y)^2 - (1/2)(x-y)^2. Variant qfgaussred_positive assumes positive definite form, is faster and returns NULL if negative norm occurs. Syntax: qfgaussred(GEN q).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfisom(G, H, {fl})
rubrics_metrics.description: Find invertible S such that G = tS H S (isomorphism between lattices represented by positive definite integer symmetric matrices G and H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be slow as it computes minimal vectors. G can be a qfisominit structure for repeated comparisons. Implements algorithm of Plesken & Souvignier. Syntax: qfisom0(GEN G, GEN H, GEN fl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfisominit(G, {fl})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return an 'isom' structure for G (positive definite integer symmetric matrix) to speed up later isomorphism computations to other forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: fl, if present, is a t_VEC with two components: fl[1] = depth of scalar product combination to use; fl[2] = maximum level of Bacher polynomials. Interface experimental; computations can be lengthy for large dimension. Syntax: qfisominit0(GEN G, GEN fl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfjacobi(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Jacobi's eigenvalue algorithm to real symmetric matrix A, returning [L,V] with L sorted eigenvalues and V the orthogonal eigenvector matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show precision and orthogonality checks. Syntax: jacobi(GEN A, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qflll(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply LLL algorithm to columns of matrix x returning unimodular transformation T so x·T is an LLL-reduced basis; columns may be dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default LLL parameters are (0.51,0.99). flag bits: 0 = assume exact or real entries (rescaled to integers), 1 = assume integral (approximate Gram-Schmidt with adaptive precision), 2 = partially reduced basis algorithm (fast for knapsack-type lattices but not LLL-reduced), 4 = return [K,T] where K basis of integer kernel and T transforms image to LLL-reduced basis, 5 = like 4 but polynomial coeffs allowed, 8 = like 0 but polynomial coeffs allowed. Alternatives: lll (flag=0), lllint (flag=1), lllkerim (flag=4). Implementations adapted from fplll/Nguyen-Stehlé and Montgomery for flag=2.

rubrics_metrics.name: qflllgram(G, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: LLL reduction when input is Gram matrix G = x~ * x (square symmetric real, positive quadratic form not necessarily definite). Returns unimodular T so x·T is an LLL-reduced basis of lattice generated by columns of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag semantics similar to qflll: 0 = exact/real entries; 1 = integral with approximate Gram-Schmidt; 4 = integer entries, gives kernel and reduced image; 5 = like 4 but polynomial coeffs accepted. Syntax: qflllgram0(GEN G, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfminim(x, {b}, {m}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerate vectors of quadratic form x (positive definite symmetric matrix) whose norm ≤ b using Fincke-Pohst; store at most m vectors (no limit if m omitted). If b omitted, search minimal non-zero vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag behavior: 0 (default) seeks at most 2m vectors and returns [#found, max_norm, matrix_of_vectors]; 1 ignores m and returns [N,v] (a non-zero vector of length N ≤ b or []); in flags 0/1 x must be integral and routine uses low-precision floating computations for speed (may error if large rounding errors). flag=2: x can have non-integral real entries; behavior more robust but slower; if m omitted all found vectors are stored (may be huge). Examples include Leech lattice enumeration and advice about pairsize memory. Syntax: qfminim0(GEN x, GEN b = NULL, GEN m = NULL, long flag, long prec). Also minim, minim2, minim_raw alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfnorm(x, {q})
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate binary quadratic form q at vector x (defaults to Euclidean form). Equivalent to x~ * q * x but faster; accepts matrices and returns Gram matrix for t_MATs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and timing comparisons given. Polar form available via qfbil. Syntax: qfnorm(GEN x, GEN q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfperfection(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the perfection rank of quadratic form G (rank of family of symmetric matrices v_i v_i^t where v_i run over minimal vectors; s is half number of minimal vectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires computing minimal vectors and can become very lengthy as dimension grows. Syntax: perf(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfrep(q, B, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Count vectors representing successive integers by quadratic form q (positive definite integer symmetric matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 counts all vectors and returns vector whose i-th entry (1 ≤ i ≤ B) is half the number of vectors v with q(v)=i. flag=1 counts vectors of even norm and returns vector with entry i equal to half number of v such that q(v)=2i. Uses naive algorithm based on qfminim and will fail if entries exceed 2^31 (or 2^63). Syntax: qfrep0(GEN q, GEN B, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfsign(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return [p,m], the signature of quadratic form represented by symmetric matrix x: number of positive (p) and negative (m) eigenvalues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed using Gaussian reduction. Syntax: qfsign(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: seralgdep(s, p, r)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a linear relation between powers (1, s, ..., s^p) of series s with polynomial coefficients of degree ≤ r; return 0 if none found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows polynomial in x with coefficients in series in y; series main variable must not be x to express result as polynomial in x. Syntax: seralgdep(GEN s, long p, long r).

rubrics_metrics.name: setbinop(f, X, {Y})
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct the set { f(x,y) : x in X, y in Y } (if Y omitted, assume X=Y and f symmetric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: set addition and subtraction of sets. Syntax: setbinop(GEN f, GEN X, GEN Y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: setintersect(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection of two sets x and y (in PARI, a set is a strictly increasing row vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result undefined if x or y is not a set. Use Set to convert other objects to sets. Syntax: setintersect(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setisset(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return true (1) if x is a PARI set, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: in PARI a set is a row vector with strictly increasing entries under PARI's universal comparison. Use Set(x) to convert vectors/lists to a set (removes duplicates and sorts). Syntax: setisset(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: setminus(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set difference: elements of x that are not in y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undefined if x or y is not a set. Syntax: setminus(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setsearch(S, x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine membership of x in set S. If flag=0 (default) return index j with S[j]=x or 0 if not present; if flag≠0 return insertion index where x should be inserted (0 if already present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default behavior requires that S is a PARI set (strictly increasing row vector). For non-sets, may work on sorted lists (lists sorted with listsort(L,1)). Examples show pitfalls when input not set/sorted. Syntax: setsearch(GEN S, GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: setunion(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Union of sets x and y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undefined if x or y is not a set. Syntax: setunion(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: trace(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized trace: for a square matrix ordinary trace; for non-matrix it's sum with conjugate; for polmods it's algebraic number trace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x is non-square matrix (but not a vector), an error occurs. Syntax: gtrace(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecextract(x, y, {z})
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract components of vector/matrix x according to component specifier y (and optional column specifier z for matrices). y can be integer mask, integer vector of indices, or string describing range or complement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mask: binary digits of integer read right-to-left correspond to components left-to-right. Vector y gives explicit indices in given order. String options: 'a..b' with omitted a or b defaulting to 1 or -1; negative indices count from end; leading '^' takes complement; reverse order supported in string ranges. Range notation v[i..j] and M[i..j,k..l] is faster but lacks reverse order and omitted endpoints. Syntax: extract0(GEN x, GEN y, GEN z = NULL). Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsearch(v, x, {cmpf})
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for x in a sorted vector or list v: return index where found or 0 if absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cmpf omitted v assumed sorted in increasing order by standard comparator (restricting types). If cmpf present, v must be sorted accordingly. v may be a matrix (seen as vector of columns) and x may be a column vector or its transpose. Result undefined for unsorted v. Syntax: vecsearch(GEN v, GEN x, GEN cmpf = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsort(x, {cmpf}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort vector/list/matrix columns x in ascending order using mergesort (stable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cmpf omitted uses standard lexicographic comparator (restricting types). cmpf can be integer k (sort by k-th subcomponent), a vector (lexicographic ordering by listed components), or a comparison function closure (x,y)->int. flag bits: 1 = indirect sort (return permutation); 4 = descending order; 8 = remove duplicates w.r.t comparator (keep first). Examples show sorting by custom functions and efficiency tips (precompute expensive keys). Syntax: vecsort0(GEN x, GEN cmpf = NULL, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsum(v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the sum of components of vector v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trivial utility; syntax: vecsum(GEN v).

rubrics_metrics.name: vector(n, {X}, {expr = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a row vector (t_VEC) of length n whose i-th component is expr evaluated at X taking values 1..n; defaults to zeros if optional args omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: X is lexically scoped per evaluation (local to each element) so changes inside expr do not affect next iterations; examples illustrate per-element scoping vs for-loops. Syntax: vector(n, X, expr).

rubrics_metrics.name: vectorsmall(n, {X}, {expr = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like vector but returns a t_VECSMALL (row vector of small integers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same per-element scoping and defaults as vector. Syntax analogous.

rubrics_metrics.name: vectorv(n, {X}, {expr = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like vector but returns a column vector (t_COL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same semantics as vector; use when a column vector is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical integration overview (intnum/intnumromb and double-exponential)
rubrics_metrics.description: intnum implements double-exponential univariate integration (since v2.2.9) and supersedes Romberg (intnumromb). Can compute integrals to thousands of decimals for regular integrands; supports non-compact domains and certain endpoint singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User must split integrals into subintegrals with no interior singularities; polynomials in logs are not considered singular; allowed singularities are algebraic at endpoints or simple derivative discontinuities; abs(x) is singular at 0. For library mode, functions are coded as eval(E,x) with signature provided. See later sum/integration functions for specific interfaces and tab/intnuminit usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: derivnum(X = a, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical derivative of expr with respect to X at X=a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows high precision agreement. In library mode, signature derivnum(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, long prec). derivfun variant allows power series for a.

rubrics_metrics.name: intcirc(X = a, R, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of (2iπ)^{-1} expr with respect to X around circle |X-a|=R (computes sum of residues for meromorphic functions inside disk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tab parameter like intnum (if computed with intnuminit, endpoints should be [-1,1]). Example shows zeta integration. Library signature intcirc(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN R, GEN tab, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: intfouriercos(X = a, b, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of expr(X) cos(2π z X) from a to b: Fourier cosine transform over [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints coded as in intnum; a,b may be infinite but then oscillation markers are forbidden. Signature intfouriercos(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN b, GEN z, GEN tab, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: intfourierexp(X = a, b, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of expr(X) exp(-2iπ z X) from a to b: Fourier transform (note minus sign) over [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints coded as in intnum; infinite endpoints disallow oscillation markers. Signature intfourierexp(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN b, GEN z, GEN tab, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: intfouriersin(X = a, b, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of expr(X) sin(2π z X) from a to b: Fourier sine transform over [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints coded as in intnum; infinite endpoints disallow oscillation markers. Signature intfouriersin(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN b, GEN z, GEN tab, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: intfuncinit(X = a, b, expr, {flag = 0}, {m = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize tables for integral transforms (e.g., intmellininv) where s(X)=expr multiplies integration weights; useful when s(X) is expensive to compute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag≠0, assumes s(-X)=s(X) (even), making computation twice as fast. m as in intnuminit. Library signature differs order of m and flag: intfuncinit(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN b, long m, long flag, long prec). See intmellininvshort examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: intlaplaceinv(X = sig, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical inverse Laplace transform: integrate (2iπ)^{-1} expr(X) e^{X z} along line Re(X)=sig to evaluate inverse Laplace at z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: sig can be real σ (abscissa) or vector [σ, α] where α=0 for slowly decreasing integrands or α>0 for exp(-α t) decay (not necessary to choose exact α). tab as in intnum. Practical advice: increasing m (intnumstep) or σ often improves accuracy; examples show tradeoff between time and precision. Library signature intlaplaceinv(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN sig, GEN z, ...).
